ai.title: Freebuff E2E CI workflow and test suite
ai.summary: Added GitHub Actions workflow `.github/workflows/freebuff-e2e.yml` to run E2E tests on every commit to `main` and PRs. Tests use `tmux` to drive the compiled Freebuff binary, covering startup, slash commands, code editing, and agent behavior. New utilities in `freebuff/e2e/utils/` handle binary resolution and session management. An optional SDK-driven agent tester (`freebuff/e2e/agent/freebuff-tester.ts`) verifies complex interactions using `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`.

eli5.text: Every time a developer changes the code for the Freebuff application, an automated system now runs a full set of tests that simulate real usage - it actually starts up the program, types in commands, edits code, and checks that everything works as expected. This happens automatically for every proposed change before it gets merged, and it even uses an AI helper to verify more complex behaviors. You wouldn't notice this directly unless you're submitting code changes, but it means bugs are caught before they reach you.

ai.title: Remove mode-restriction e2e test from CI
ai.summary: Removed `mode-restriction` from the matrix in `.github/workflows/freebuff-e2e.yml`. This prunes the specific test case from the end-to-end suite execution. Scope limited to CI configuration.

eli5.text: The automated test that checked how the assistant handles mode restrictions has been turned off in the continuous integration system. This affects only the internal testing pipeline, not any user-facing feature. If you looked at the test configuration, you would notice that the mode restriction test case is no longer listed among the scenarios being validated automatically.

ai.title: Add Browser Use agent
ai.summary: New agent definition `agents/browser-use/browser-use.ts` enables browser automation via Chrome DevTools MCP server. Uses `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview` model. Requires local Chrome installation; MCP server auto-downloads via `npx`. Structured output schema includes `overallStatus`, `results`, `consoleErrors`, and `lessons`.

eli5.text: An AI assistant can now drive a web browser for you: it loads pages, clicks buttons, fills in forms, and reads what went wrong, all without you typing. You just describe the task (for example, checking that a login form works on a website) and the assistant reports back what it saw, including any errors the browser logged. This works today if you have Chrome installed on your computer. The browser-automation feature is now available as one of the built-in assistants you can ask to test websites and web apps.

ai.title: browser-use subagent gated on chrome detection
ai.summary: Added `browser-use` to the `base2` agent list, gated by `chromeAvailable` in `ProjectFileContext`. `system-info.ts` implements `findChromeExecutable` to check standard install paths, updating `getSystemInfo` to return the boolean. `prompts.ts` injects 'Chrome: installed/not found' into the system prompt, allowing the base agent to skip spawning `browser-use` if Chrome is missing. `run-state.ts` uses the shared `getSystemInfo` helper.

eli5.text: The assistant can now offer to control a web browser as one of its helper tools, but only if Google Chrome is actually installed on your computer. Before it tries to start that browser tool, it will quickly check your system and, if it can't find Chrome, it will skip that option and tell you instead. You'd only notice this new choice when you ask the assistant to do something that involves browsing the web, and you'd see it work or get a message saying Chrome is missing. This is live as of 2026-03-15.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.16 release packaging bump
ai.summary: Bumped the Freebuff package version from 0.0.15 to 0.0.16 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` as part of release packaging. This single-line version increment tags the accumulated changes in the release line, including the new Browser Use agent with Chrome-gated spawning, the end-to-end CI workflow driven via `tmux`, reordering of `/interview` above `/plan` in the CLI command registry, and the terminal UI `ShimmerText` "working..." animation in collapsed agent branches. The bump reflects the canonical Freebuff Monorepo Architecture surface entry point defined by the packaged CLI binary.
ai.evidence: The diff in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` increments the `version` field from `0.0.15` to `0.0.16`, constituting a release-bump commit. The commit metadata confirms Release instructions: this row is a version bump.

eli5.text: This release adds a new browser automation agent and makes the tool more reliable. Freebuff now includes a built-in web browser agent that can drive a real Chrome browser to help with web-based tasks, using a new AI model. The browser feature automatically checks if Chrome is installed, so it only appears when it can actually work. A continuous testing system now runs behind the scenes on every update, helping to catch bugs earlier and keep the software stable. Upgrading gives you smoother, more dependable performance and access to web browsing automation when Chrome is available on your computer.

ai.title: Add e2e:knowledge-file npm script
ai.summary: Added `e2e:knowledge-file` script to `freebuff/package.json` executing `bun test e2e/tests/knowledge-file.e2e.test.ts`. Extends e2e test surface to cover knowledge file behavior. Aligns with existing `e2e:ads`, `e2e:agent`, `e2e:code-edit`, and `e2e:terminal-command` patterns.

eli5.text: The assistant's testing toolkit now includes a check specifically for how it handles knowledge files. If someone runs the full set of automated end-to-end tests, a new scenario will launch the assistant to confirm it can load and use a knowledge file correctly. This fills a gap in the existing test coverage alongside the tests already in place for agent startup, ads, code editing, and terminal commands.

ai.title: Add CanopyWave prompt caching benchmark
ai.summary: Adds `scripts/test-canopywave-long.ts` to benchmark CanopyWave prompt caching across 10-turn conversations using a ~5k token system prompt and `minimax/minimax-m2.5`. Updates `scripts/test-siliconflow.ts` to read `SILICON_FLOW_API_KEY` instead of `SILICONFLOW_API_KEY`. Internal tooling only.

eli5.text: A new internal test was added that measures how well a specific AI model caches large shared instructions across a 10-question conversation. Engineers can now run this test to see how much of the repeated prompt gets reused (and how much they save) when using the minimax model via the CanopyWave provider. One test script was also updated to read its secret API key from a slightly differently named environment variable, so anyone running that script needs to make sure that variable is set with the new name. Both changes are internal tooling only and are not visible to end users.

ai.title: Add working... shimmer to subagents
ai.summary: The `agent-branch-item.tsx` component now renders a `ShimmerText` "working..." animation when `isStreaming` is true. This provides visual feedback that a subagent is actively processing. The change applies to the CLI interface, specifically within the agent branch UI blocks. The shimmer interval is set to 160ms using the theme's secondary color.

eli5.text: You now see a shimmering 'working...' label under any subagent that is actively running, so you can tell it hasn't frozen. The animation only appears while that specific subagent is processing, and uses a soft secondary color to match the rest of the interface. It's live today, so you'll see it immediately whenever you launch a subagent that is still thinking or working.

ai.title: Rename commander and commander-lite agents to basher
ai.summary: The `commander` and `commander-lite` agents were consolidated and renamed to `basher`. This removes the free-tier variant distinction, using a single lightweight shell command executor backed by `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview`. Updates propagate to agent registries, CLI display constants, and prompt instructions across core and CLI packages. Legacy `commander-lite` references are removed from free agent model maps.

eli5.text: When you (or the assistant) ask the system to run a terminal command through an agent, it now goes to a single agent called "basher" instead of picking between "commander" on paid plans and "commander-lite" on free plans. The change renames the agent, deletes the free-tier copy entirely, and updates all the help text and internal references so the two old names are gone everywhere you'd look or be told to use. Behind the scenes, "basher" is built from the same lightweight code as the old "commander-lite" and runs commands the same way, so the behavior you get is unchanged - the only visible difference is the new name in menus, instructions, and error messages. The developers note this is live in the current build and that "basher" is the real agent name you must reference (not a tool) when

ai.title: Hide streaming indicator in collapsed agent branches
ai.summary: The streaming text indicator now requires isExpanded to render. Prevents visual clutter in collapsed agent branches. Scope: cli/src/components/blocks/agent-branch-item.tsx.

eli5.text: If you collapse an agent branch so it's folded up, the little 'working...' streaming text now stays hidden instead of showing. You'd notice this only when looking at subagents in the CLI: previously the streaming indicator appeared even when the branch was collapsed, now it waits until you expand that branch first. The change is live today and affects anyone viewing agent branches in the terminal.

ai.title: waitForReady added to FreebuffSession e2e helper
ai.summary: Added waitForReady method to FreebuffSession in freebuff/e2e/utils/freebuff-session.ts. This helper polls terminal output to ensure the TUI renders its initial layout before tests proceed. It checks for a minimum number of non-empty lines, with configurable timeout and line count. This stabilizes e2e tests by preventing race conditions during CLI startup.

eli5.text: When you launch the software, your screen stays blank for a moment before the menus and text appear. If a test tried to interact with the screen during that split second, it could fail because nothing was visible yet. Now, before any test begins, the system pauses and waits until the screen shows enough lines of text (at least five) to confirm it's fully loaded. This prevents those premature failures and makes the tests run reliably every time. There's nothing for you to click or enable; this works automatically whenever you use the software.

ai.title: Upgrade @opentui/core and @opentui/react to 0.1.87
ai.summary: Upgraded @opentui/core and @opentui/react from 0.1.74 to 0.1.87. This change affects the CLI's terminal UI rendering capabilities. The update ensures compatibility with the latest features and bug fixes in the OpenTUI libraries.

eli5.text: The CLI's text-based interface (the part you see in your terminal when you run commands) received a behind-the-scenes upgrade to its rendering library. This means the text display is now powered by a newer version of the OpenTUI libraries, which should help keep everything working correctly and compatible with future updates. There's nothing new you'd directly notice as a feature, but the terminal output may render slightly more reliably. This change is now live in the current version of the CLI.

ai.title: Move /interview above /plan in CLI command registry
ai.summary: Reordered `interview` command definition to precede `plan` in `cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts` and `cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts`. This adjustment places the interview workflow earlier in the command list, likely prioritizing spec-generation over planning in the default UI or autocomplete order. The change affects CLI command registration and slash command metadata, ensuring consistent ordering across surfaces.

eli5.text: When you type a slash command in the CLI, the assistant's question-gathering command now appears before the planning command in the autocomplete list. This means if you start typing a slash command, you'll see the interview option listed above the plan option. The assistant can now guide you through a series of questions to flesh out your request into a spec before you jump to planning, making it easier to start conversations that need more detail.

ai.title: Fix freebuff e2e tests
ai.summary: Updated e2e test utilities to improve stability and branding verification. `waitForReady` timeout increased from 15s to 30s in `freebuff-session.ts`. `tmux-custom-tools.ts` now calls `waitForReady` before capturing initial output. `freebuff-tester.ts` prompt updated to check for visible startup content instead of specific 'Freebuff' branding.

eli5.text: When Freebuff's automated end-to-end tests start up the program, they wait longer before checking the screen, up to 30 seconds instead of 15, so startup on slower machines no longer fails the test. The tests no longer look specifically for the word 'Freebuff' in the initial display; since Freebuff was forked from Codebuff, the old branding check could match the wrong program, so the checker now just confirms the startup screen actually shows something rather than being blank. If you watched a test run, you would see it wait patiently after launch and then pass even when the startup was slow, instead of rushing and failing on a half-rendered screen.
